sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Differentiate between the MIN() and MAX() functions.
questions.answer: MIN() returns the smallest number in a set of values, e.g. =MIN(B2:B6) gives the lowest mark. MAX() returns the largest number, e.g. =MAX(B2:B6) gives the highest mark. Both accept up to 255 arguments.

questions.q: What is the SUMIF() function? Give its syntax.
questions.answer: SUMIF adds only those cells that meet a given condition. Syntax: SUMIF(range, criteria, sum_range). Example: =SUMIF(B3:E3, ">99") adds only the values greater than 99; blank and text cells are ignored.

questions.q: Differentiate between formulas and functions.
questions.answer: A formula is an expression written by the user, starting with =, using operators and cell references, e.g. =B3+C3+D3. A function is a built-in formula with a name, to which you give arguments in parentheses, e.g. =SUM(B3:D3) or =AVERAGE(B3:D3).

questions.q: What are the elements of a formula in an Excel spreadsheet?
questions.answer: A formula must begin with the = sign and can contain mathematical operators (+, −, *, /) and logical operators (<, >), cell references (including named ranges), text or values, and worksheet functions such as SUM and AVERAGE.

questions.q: What is a legend in a chart?
questions.answer: A legend is the chart component that shows the colour, symbol or pattern used to mark each data series, so the reader knows which bar, line or slice stands for which data.

questions.q: What is SmartArt? Write the steps to create a SmartArt graphic.
questions.answer: SmartArt is a visual representation of information and ideas (list, process, cycle, hierarchy, relationship). Steps: Insert tab → Illustrations → SmartArt → choose a category and layout → OK → click each shape and type the text.

questions.q: Differentiate between AutoShapes and SmartArt graphics.
questions.answer: AutoShapes are ready-made shapes — lines, arrows, basic shapes, flowchart symbols, stars and callouts — drawn one by one. SmartArt creates a complete diagram of ideas, such as a process or hierarchy, from a chosen layout into which text is typed.

questions.q: Differentiate between a bar chart and an area chart.
questions.answer: A bar chart uses horizontal bars to compare individual items. An area chart plots data as a filled area to highlight the degree of change over time and draw attention to the total value across a trend.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain any five components of a chart.
questions.answer: (1) Chart title — the title of the whole chart. (2) Axis titles — names of the X-axis and Y-axis data. (3) X-axis categories and Y-axis values — the categories plotted and the value scale. (4) Legend — colour or pattern used for each data series. (5) Data labels — the values of the data plotted. Also tick marks (scale of axes) and gridlines (lines at major intervals).

questions.q: Write the steps to plot a pie chart with the title 'First Quarter Sales' for given sales data.
questions.answer: (1) Enter the item names in column A and sales percentages in column B. (2) Select the data range A1:B6. (3) Insert tab → Charts group → Pie → choose a sub-type (2-D Pie). (4) Click the chart → Chart Tools Layout → Chart Title → Above Chart. (5) Type 'First Quarter Sales'. (6) Add data labels from Layout → Data Labels if needed.

questions.q: A table shows marks in 5 subjects. Write the steps to create a line chart titled 'Performance Analysis' with X-axis 'Subject' and Y-axis 'Score'.
questions.answer: (1) Enter subjects in column A and marks in column B; select the range. (2) Insert → Charts → Line → choose a sub-type. (3) Layout → Chart Title → type 'Performance Analysis'. (4) Layout → Axis Titles → Primary Horizontal Axis Title → type 'Subject'. (5) Layout → Axis Titles → Primary Vertical Axis Title → type 'Score'.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is a chart? Explain any four types of charts available in Excel.
questions.answer: A chart is a visual representation of worksheet data that makes comparisons and trends easy to see. (1) Column chart — vertical bars compare values across categories. (2) Line chart — shows trends over equal intervals of time. (3) Pie chart — shows the proportion of each part to the whole; one data series, best with 5–6 slices. (4) Bar chart — horizontal bars compare individual items. Others: Area (change over time and total), XY Scatter (relationship between two variables), Stock (price fluctuations), Surface, Doughnut, Bubble and Radar.

or.q: Write the steps to draw a chart in Excel 2007 and give it titles.
or.answer: (1) Enter the data in the worksheet. (2) Select the data range with the mouse. (3) Insert tab → Charts group → choose a chart type. (4) Choose the sub-type; the chart appears. (5) Click the chart → Chart Tools Layout → Chart Title → type a title. (6) Layout → Axis Titles → Primary Horizontal Axis Title and Primary Vertical Axis Title → type them. (7) Use Legend, Data Labels and Gridlines in the Layout tab to edit; drag handles to resize and the border to move.

questions.q: Explain the SUM, SUMIF, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN and COUNT functions with examples.
questions.answer: SUM adds numbers: =SUM(B2:B6). SUMIF adds cells meeting a condition: =SUMIF(B2:B6, ">50"). AVERAGE gives the arithmetic mean: =AVERAGE(B2:B6). MAX gives the largest value: =MAX(B2:B6). MIN gives the smallest value: =MIN(B2:B6). COUNT counts cells with numbers: =COUNT(B2:B6) (COUNTA counts non-empty cells, COUNTBLANK empty ones, COUNTIF cells meeting a condition). Each function takes up to 255 arguments, written in parentheses after the name, starting with =.
